deep.reconstruction:
Context. This leaf belongs to the working papers for Riemann's 1861 memoir 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoides' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 9, 1861). The next page is fair copy of §6 to §7 of that memoir. It covers the sign of the pressure quantity σ and the 'second case', in which two of the pairs (u,u'), (v,v'), (w,w') vanish. In that memoir a,b,c are the semi-axes. The quantities u,v,w and u',v',w' are Riemann's combinations of the angular-velocity and vorticity components about the principal axes, rescaled by factors (b-c), (b+c), etc. Most of the page is written upside down. The upright notes at the top are a separate, unrelated computation.

A. Upright fragments at the top.
(i) An operator expression like ∂(b-c)/∂t·∂u/∂t + ∂²(b-c)/∂t²·u + ..., with a term 4g(1-z²) beneath it. This looks like the start of differentiating the time equation for (b-c)u in the ellipsoid problem; it is not carried further.
(ii) A polynomial or series identity g' + h'z² = 12z⁴ - 12z⁶ + y(1-z²)(z³ + 3z⁵ + ...). Its purpose cannot be determined from the page; it seems to be a coefficient comparison in a power series in z.

B. Main (inverted) block: steady motions with constant axes.
1. Riemann writes the equations of motion for the rotation quantities with the time derivatives of a,b set to zero. This is the case of a figure of constant shape, with the c-axis singled out or c = b. The resulting linear relations have the schematic form (my reconstruction of the badly legible lines):
   ∂t/∂(a+b)·v² + ∂t/∂(b-a)·w² + ... = 0,
   (a-b)∂/∂a(...)·w + ... + (a+b)uv = 0,
   (b+a)∂/∂b(...)·v + ... + (b-a)uw = 0.
   In the constant-axis case these reduce to bilinear algebraic conditions such as (b-a)uw + (b+a)u'v' = 0, together with analogous conditions in which w,v are interchanged with their primed partners.
2. He also records the trivial solution v = w = 0 (with u = 0), i.e. rotation about a single principal axis. This is the 'second case' treated on the next page, giving the integrals (a-b)²w = τ and (a+b)²w' = τ'.
3. He then forms combinations of these conditions. One such combination is
   ∂t/∂(b-a)·(v/w + w/v) - ∂t/∂(b+a)·(w/v + v/w) = 0.
   He also derives proportionalities between the mixed quantities: v/u = w'/v' and v'/u' = -w/v, and hence v/u - w/v = v'/w' - u'/v'.
4. Two alternatives are marked I and II:
   I: u w' = w u',
   II: v u' + u v' = 0.
   Each comes with quadratic constraints:
   (b-a)u² + (b+a)u'² = 0, which forces u = u' = 0 if b > a > 0, and
   (b-a)w² = (b+a)v², i.e. w/v = ±√((b+a)/(b-a)).
   He also obtains
   (b-a)(v² - w²) + (b+a)(v'² - w'²) = 0 and (b-a)v² - (b+a)w² = 0.
   [My inference] Combining (b-a)v² = (b+a)w² with (b-a)w² = (b+a)v² gives -2a(v² + w²) = 0. So for a ≠ 0 we get v = w = 0, which is the reduction to the single-axis case.
5. Side remarks: 'c = b, ab = const' and '(b-a)/(b+a) = const' look like tests of special subcases, such as a spheroid-like case, or similarity of the a,b cross-section in time. The marginal formula (b-a)w² = (b+a)v²·const ties the bookkeeping to the integrals (b-a)²w = τ.
   Overall the block is a case analysis of when the dynamical system admits steady motions with fixed axes. Riemann's published conclusion is that either the rotation is about a principal axis, or the rotation axis and vorticity lie in a principal plane (his cases I, II, III, the Riemann ellipsoids).

C. Bottom: separation of variables for a Laplacian or Helmholtz-type equation.
Set u = r^h v. Then
   ∂u/∂r = r^h v_r + h r^(h-1) v,
   ∂²u/∂r² = r^h v_rr + 2h r^(h-1) v_r + h(h-1) r^(h-2) v.
The first line, written as ∂²u/∂z² in the transcription, should be the radial part of the Laplacian, ∂²u/∂r² + (2/r)∂u/∂r. It equals r^h v_rr + (2h+2) r^(h-1) v_r + h(h+1) r^(h-2) v.
The angular part is (1/sinθ)∂(sinθ ∂u/∂θ)/∂θ + ... = λu, i.e. the Legendre eigenvalue problem. There is a one-dimensional analogue ∂²u/∂z² = α²u, a struck-out rescaled equation ∂²u/∂x² = α²·... + ∂²u/∂y² + ∂²u/∂z², and a substitution ξ = √π x. This is routine separation in spherical coordinates, probably unrelated to the ellipsoid problem or an aside on ellipsoidal or spherical potentials.
errors: The first line of the bottom derivative block is labelled ∂²u/∂z² (as transcribed). Its right-hand side r^h v'' + (2h+2) r^(h-1) v' + h(h+1) r^(h-2) v is actually ∂²u/∂r² + (2/r)∂u/∂r, the radial Laplacian. The label is either a misreading or a slip of notation; the formula itself is correct.
The second line, r^h v'' + 2h r^(h-1) v' + h(h-1) r^(h-2) v, is correct for ∂²u/∂r².
The first-derivative line is correct; the transcribed 'r^h ∂v/∂r + h r^(h-1) v' has a struck-out stray fragment.

In the steady-state block several lines are fragmentary. In particular, (b-a)u² + (b+a)u'² = 0 has only the trivial real solution when b > a > 0, so Riemann is presumably ruling a branch out rather than asserting a nontrivial relation.

The struck-out line ∂²u/∂x² = ... and the formula with α²∂²u/∂z² + ∂²u/∂y² + ∂²u/∂z² (as transcribed) are inconsistent as written, with ∂²u/∂z² appearing twice. This is probably a misreading or abandoned scratch.

results.what: Case analysis of steady (constant-axis) motions of a self-gravitating homogeneous liquid ellipsoid with internal vorticity: algebraic conditions on u,v,w,u',v',w', and reduction to rotation about a principal axis (v=w=0) or about axes in a principal plane
results.modern_name: Riemann ellipsoids (classification of Riemann's types S, I, II, III)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1861), building on Dirichlet, Dedekind, Jacobi and MacLaurin; later systematized by Chandrasekhar (1965-69)

results.what: Integrals for rotation about one principal axis: (a-b)²w = τ, (a+b)²w' = τ'
results.modern_name: Conservation of angular momentum and circulation (Kelvin) for Dirichlet-Dedekind-Riemann ellipsoids

results.what: Substitution u = r^h v in the radial Laplacian, plus the Legendre angular operator eigenproblem
results.modern_name: Separation of variables in spherical coordinates / spherical harmonics

deep.surprise_reason: These are draft computations for Riemann's own published 1861 memoir on the liquid ellipsoid (the next page is its fair copy), plus routine separation-of-variables formulas. Nothing here goes beyond what is published and credited to him.

checkable.asserts: The radial Laplacian of u = r^h v equals r^h v'' + (2h+2) r^(h-1) v' + h(h+1) r^(h-2) v (should give 0).
The second r-derivative of r^h v (should give 0).
Adding (b-a)v² = (b+a)w² and (b-a)w² = (b+a)v² gives -2a(v²+w²), so both relations together force v = w = 0 for a ≠ 0.
The rotation quantity w is determined by the constant τ via (a-b)²w = τ (single-axis case integral).

transcription_corrections: Most of the page is written upside down; the machine reading of those lines is very uncertain. Many of the 'ỏt/∂(...)' symbols are probably ∂/∂t or partial derivatives of the axes, not of a variable t.
The line labelled '∂²u/∂z² = r^h ∂²v/∂r² + (2h+2) r^(h-1) ∂v/∂r + h(h+1) r^(h-2) v' should be read as the radial Laplacian ∂²u/∂r² + (2/r)∂u/∂r; the next line should be labelled ∂²u/∂r².
'(b-a)uw + (b+a)vw' = 0' in the upper block is probably '(b-a)uw + (b+a)u'v' = 0' (primed partners), matching the later line.
'(b-a)u² + (b+a)u'² = 0' may instead be '(b-a)u² + (b+a)u'² ...' in the form of a ratio condition; it is too faint to confirm.
The 'y' in 'g' + h'z² = ... + y(1-zz)(...)' is likely 4 or g; uncertain.
